question: Which ministry is responsible for implementing DISHA?

options.text: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (Meity)

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Rural Development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DISHA (District Development Coordination and Monitoring Committee):** DISHA is a platform launched by the Government of India to ensure effective coordination and monitoring of government schemes and programs implemented in the districts. It aims to improve development outcomes by facilitating better coordination among various stakeholders.
 
• The **Ministry of Rural Development** is primarily responsible for implementing DISHA. This ministry plays a crucial role in ensuring the proper execution of rural development schemes and programs across the country.
 
• DISHA committees are formed at the district level. These committees are responsible for monitoring the implementation of government schemes and ensuring the efficient use of resources for development purposes.
 
• The primary goal of DISHA is to ensure transparency, accountability, and efficiency in the implementation of government programs. It provides a platform for elected representatives, government officials, and other stakeholders to work together to achieve developmental goals.
 
• The DISHA platform includes schemes related to various sectors, such as rural development, health, education, and infrastructure. Its activities focus on enhancing the quality of life in rural areas.
 
• The Ministry of Rural Development provides guidelines, training, and resources to state and district-level authorities for the effective functioning of DISHA committees. The ministry also monitors the progress and outcomes of DISHA-related activities.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is the Ministry of Rural Development.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of DISHA:**

 
 
• The primary objective of DISHA is to ensure the effective implementation of central government schemes at the district level. It seeks to eliminate bottlenecks and enhance the delivery of services to beneficiaries.
 
• It ensures that the benefits of schemes reach the intended beneficiaries, particularly in rural and underdeveloped areas. This is achieved by increasing coordination among district-level authorities.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of DISHA:**
 
 
• DISHA includes elected representatives such as MPs and MLAs in its committees to ensure political accountability and transparency in decision-making.
 
• It monitors a wide range of schemes, including flagship programs like **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS)**, **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)**, and **National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP)**.
 
• The platform uses technology and data analytics to track the progress of schemes and identify areas for improvement.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Ministry of Rural Development:**
 
 
• The ministry ensures that DISHA committees are functional and effective in all districts. It provides guidelines and support to district administrations for conducting meetings and preparing action plans.
 
• The ministry also collaborates with other ministries and state governments to ensure the smooth implementation of DISHA-related activities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Stakeholders in DISHA Committees:**

 
 
• The committees are chaired by Members of Parliament (MPs) from the respective districts. District Magistrates or Collectors act as the Member Secretaries of the committees.
 
• Other members include elected representatives such as MLAs, local government officials, and representatives from civil society organizations.
 
 
 
• **Significance of DISHA:**
 
 
• DISHA enhances accountability in the implementation of government schemes and ensures that resources are utilized effectively. It helps in identifying and addressing issues related to service delivery.
 
• It also promotes transparency by involving elected representatives and other stakeholders in the decision-making process.
